decision.summary: Two regions stand out: (1) a coherent multi-axis offset near indices 485–492 featuring a large U drop and smaller N/E steps; (2) a very sharp U drop near 605–612 with supporting N/E changes. Both show abrupt multi-sample transitions and sustained offsets, not resolvable as single-sample spikes. Other segments exhibit ordinary noise or smooth motion.

regions.observation: Sharp ~10 mm downward step in U (centered MAD) at index ~488–490, accompanied by a smaller (~4 mm) upward step in N and a modest (~2 mm) upward step in E; all three axes show a sustained offset through ~492 before possible partial return begins. The multi-axis coherence suggests a real displacement rather than noise.

Abrupt ~20 mm drop in U at index ~608–610, with concurrent ~3 mm drop in N and ~1 mm drop in E; the U component remains depressed for several samples before a slow, ambiguous recovery begins around 612. The sharpness and cross-axis consistency warrant closer inspection despite overlap with window boundary.
